gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EcoFlow sells two 1,024 Wh DELTA 3 models. Only the DELTA 3 ($579) can take extra batteries, up to 5 kWh; EcoFlow's own comparison table lists the cheaper DELTA 3 Classic ($459) as not expandable. Separately, BLUETTI's US store lists the AC200L (a card ChatGPT showed, and a model on our page) as Discontinued.
standout_why: I compared against dealectric.com (ours, cited), blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/home-oxygen-concentrator-5l (cited), willitrunpower.com (cited) and the Anker SOLIX medical-devices blog (cited in one chat). Our page says the DELTA 3 grows to 5 kWh, but it cites the DELTA 3 Plus page and never mentions the non-expandable Classic. It also says the AC200L works with the B300K only and calls it in stock, with a price from 2026-11-03. BlackoutWise covers expansion only for the F3800 Plus and DELTA Pro 3. Willrun says nothing about expansion batteries; it does cover Jackery's and EcoFlow's medical disclaimers, the Invacare extension-cord warning and switchover times, so those are not new. Anker's blog recommends only the S2000 and says nothing about expansion. None of these pages names the Classic/DELTA 3 split, the B500K's fit with the AC200L, or that the AC200L is discontinued at BLUETTI.
decides: For a 1 kWh budget pick that can grow to overnight runtime, the buyer has to get the DELTA 3, not the Classic. The Classic stays at about 2.5 h at 350 W. The DELTA 3 reaches about 12 h at 350 W with extra batteries (5,120 Wh × 0.85 / 350). The AC200L should come off the list of buy-new picks, or be marked as an existing-owner path, because BLUETTI's US store shows it as Discontinued. The page should send expandable 2 kWh buyers to an in-stock model instead.

findings.note: Same page lists 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W AC (3,600 W surge), <10 ms switchover and 12.1±0.3 kg. Runtime is fixed at about 2.5 h at 350 W (1,024 × 0.85 / 350).

findings.note: 7,577.6 Wh = 2,048 + 2 × 2,764.8 (two B300K), about 18.4 h at 350 W (× 0.85 / 350). The page says a cable is required to connect a B210. The FAQ answer on how many batteries can connect is blank.

findings.label: Anker's stated limit for medical use
findings.value: 'Never rely on a portable power station as the sole backup for life-sustaining equipment'; do not assume a consumer UPS function equals a medical-grade backup; use one only if the concentrator maker permits that backup source
findings.source_title: Portable Power Station for Medical Devices Guide - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Article dated 2026-09-18. It recommends only the SOLIX S2000 and says that is 'not presented as a medical-certified device or a guarantee of compatibility'. ChatGPT already cited this page in one chat, so it is not new.
